'''Konstantinos Tzechanis''' ({{langx|el|Κωνσταντίνος Τζεχάνης}}, {{langx|la|Constantinus Tzechani}}, {{langx|sq|Kostë Xhehani}},  1740–1800) was a [[philosopher]], [[mathematician]] and [[poet]] from the 18th century [[Aromanians|Aromanian]] center of [[Moscopole]].

==Life==
Tzechanis was born in [[Moscopole]] (Voskopojë, southeast [[Albania]]), an 18th-century cultural and commercial metropolis of the Balkans and center of Greek culture.<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Cohen|first1=Mark |title=Last century of a Sephardic community: the Jews of Monastir, 1839-1943|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=CCfXAAAAMAAJ&q=%22Education+was+so+actively+endorsed+that+Moschopolis+emerged+as+the+leading+center+of+Greek+intellectual+activity+in+the+18th%22|year=2003|publisher=Foundation for the Advancement of Sephardic Studies and Culture
|page=13|isbn=978-1-886857-06-3|quote=Moschopolis emerged as the leading center of Greek intellectual activity in the 18th century}}</ref> His ethnicity is disputed, with various sources claiming that he is of [[Albanians|Albanian]],<ref name="Clogg">{{cite book|last=Clogg|first=Richard|title=Balkan society in the age of Greek independence|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=jIWRAAAAIAAJ&q=Konstantinos+Tzechanis|accessdate=21 September 2010|year=1981|publisher=MacMillan Press|page=75|isbn=9780333315804}}</ref> [[Aromanians|Aromanian]] or [[Greeks|Greek]] origin.<ref name=Enepekides/>

Tzechanis initially studied in his home town with [[Theodore Kavalliotis]] being his teacher in the [[New Academy (Moscopole)|New Academy]]. He later attended lessons in [[Modra]], today in [[Slovakia]]. At 1760, he moved together with his parents to [[Vienna]], where his father became a merchant.<ref name=Ciesla121a>{{cite book|last1=Amburger|first1= Erik |last2= Cieśla |first2= Michał |last3= Sziklay|first3= László | title=Wissenschaftspolitik im Mittel- und Osteuropa: Wissenschaftliche Gesellschaften, Akademien und Hochschulen im 18. und beginnenden 19. Jahrhundert |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ePc2AAAAIAAJ&q=konstantinos|year=1976 |publisher=Hobbing|language=German |isbn=978-3-921515-00-6|page=121}}</ref><ref name="lloshi">{{cite book|last=Lloshi|first=Xhevat|title=Rreth Alfabetit Të Shqipes|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=9_gXTda0HS8C&q=Evstrat+Vithkuqari&pg=PA279|year=2008|publisher=Logos-A|language=Albanian|isbn=978-9989-58-268-4|page=279}}</ref><ref>[[Max Demeter Peyfuss]]. [https://books.google.com/books?id=2MxpAAAAMAAJ&q=war+gleichfalls+Moschopolit+und+kannte+KABALLIOTES%22 Die Druckerei von Moschopolis, 1731-1769: Buchdruck und Heiligenverehrung im Erzbistum Achrida]. Böhlau, 1989, {{ISBN|978-3-205-05293-7}}, p. 151 "war gleichfalls Moschopolit und kannte Kaballiotes"</ref>  Tzechanis became a teacher at the Greek schools of [[Temesvár]], [[Pest, Hungary|Pest]] and [[Zemun]].<ref name=Vakalopoulos>Apostolos Euangelou Vakalopoulos. [https://books.google.com/books?id=yOcJAQAAIAAJ ''History of Macedonia, 1354–1833'']. Institute for Balkan Studies, 1973, p. 408.</ref> Later in 1768&ndash;74 he went to [[Halle (Saale)|Halle]], then a city of the [[Kingdom of Prussia]], to study literature and mathematics, and in 1776 he studied in the [[University of Cambridge]]. He also studied in [[Leipzig]] for three years and moved to several countries of Western Europe.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Turczynski |first=Emanuel |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=J7sZAAAAIAAJ&q=%22Tzehanis,+der+%C3%BCber+drei+Jahre+in+Leipzig+studiert,+%E2%80%9ELeyden+und+Cambridge+besucht+und+Frankreich+und+Italien+besehen+hatte%22%22 |title=Die deutsch-grieschischen Kulturbeziehungen bis zur Berufung König Ottos |date=1959 |publisher=R. Oldenbourg |page=174 |language=de}}</ref> He also lived in [[Wallachia]], where he composed a satyrical poem.<ref>[https://books.google.com/books?id=dWYsAQAAIAAJ&q=%22die+Schule+besuchte%2C+dann+in+Ungarn+und+sp%C3%A4ter+in+der+Walachei+lebte%2C+wurde+durch+sein+satirisches+Gedicht+%C3%BCber+Skarlatos+Sturdza+(1771+in+Wien+gedruckt)+bekannt.%22 ''Südosteuropäische Arbeiten''], Volume 48. 1959, p. 85</ref>

In 1769 as a student he had written in Latin and Greek a treatise in geometry, the ''Introduction to Geometry: new theory of squaring the circle'', 1774 ({{langx|el|Προγύμνασμα Γεωμετρικόν, ήτοι νέα θεωρία τετραγωνισμού του κύκλου}}), in which he proposed a new theoretical solution to the problem of [[squaring the circle]].<ref name= UniofAthens/> Tzechanis also gave to the Swedish linguist [[Johann Thunmann]] a copy of ''Protopireia'', one of the most significant works of Kavalliotis,<ref>{{cite thesis |url=http://phdtheses.ekt.gr/eadd/handle/10442/1624?locale=en |title= Θεόδωρος Αναστασίου Καβαλλιώτης (1718; 1789). Ο Διδάσκαλος του Γένους |author= Κεκριδής Ευστάθιος |year= 1989 |work= [[Aristotle University of Thessaloniki]] |publisher= |accessdate=2010-09-11| pages=34–35|doi= 10.12681/eadd/1624 |type= Doctoral Dissertation |doi-access= free |url-access= subscription |hdl= 10442/hedi/1624 |hdl-access= free }}</ref> he also assisted Thunmann on his works regarding the [[Albanian language|Albanian]] and the [[Aromanian language]]s.<ref name="lloshi"/> During his stay in [[Leyden]], [[Netherlands]], Tzechanis composed two large poems in Greek, praising the local university on the one and the ancient Greek authors on the other.<ref name= UniofAthens/>

In the 1770s, he wrote in Greek a biography of [[Skanderbeg]], the national hero of Albania, based on [[Marin Barleti]]'s biography.<ref name= UniofAthens/>  He taught [[Latin language|Latin]], [[Greek language|Greek]] and mathematics in [[Leiden University]]. His best known poetry work is ''Έπος ηρωελεγείον προς Αικατερίνην'' (Heroic Epic to [[Catherine II of Russia]]), a patriotic work that aimed at the national awakening of the Greek people that lived under [[Ottoman Empire|Ottoman]] rule (1776), written in Latin and Ancient Greek and published in 1776.<ref name=Enepekides>{{cite journal | last = Enepekides | first = Polychronis K.| year = 1960| journal = Jahrbuch der österreichischen Byzantinistik| issue = 9–13 | pages = 51–57 | url = https://books.google.com/books?id=el8SAAAAIAAJ&q=tzechanis |title= Zwei Texte des 18. Jahrhunderts im Wiener Supplementum Graecum | language = German| accessdate = 2010-09-20 |publisher= H. Böhlaus}}</ref><ref>Title of the Latin version: ''Carmen heroico-elegiacum, quod temporis praesentis circumstantiarum effectum breviter expositis exponendis, humillime offert Anglis, Belgisque, philomusis generosissimis, ac studiosis nobilissimis''</ref> He died at 1800 in Leyden.<ref name= UniofAthens/>

==Work==
Tzechani composed the following works:<ref name=UniofAthens>[http://195.134.75.14/hellinomnimon/authors/New%20Bios/Tzexanis.html Τζεχάνης Κωνσταντίνος &#91;περ. 1740, Μοσχόπολη Μακεδονίας - περ. 1800, Leyden Ολλανδίας(;)&#93; ] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100930025354/http://195.134.75.14/hellinomnimon/authors/New%20Bios/Tzexanis.html |date=2010-09-30 }}. Ελληνομνήμων. University of Athens database.</ref>

*Εγχειρίδιον αριθμητικής, (Manual of Mathematics, Halle, 1769)
* Έπος ηρωελεγείον εις Βικέντιον Ιωάννοβιτζ τον Τεμεσβαρίου επίσκοπον, (Honorary poem to bishop Vincent Jovanovic, Vienna, 1772)
* Έπος εις τον κόμητα Φραγκίσκον Κολλάριον, (Epic to count Francis Collaro, 1772)
* Έπος ηρωελεγείον εις τον Κωνσταντίνον Αλέξανδρον φιλιππίδην τον Γάιον, (Honorary poem to Konstantine Alexander, 1773)
* Έπος ηρωελεγείον εις τον κραταιότατον και αήττητον των Ρωμαίων αυτοκράτορα, (Honorary poem to the mighty and invincible Emperor of the Romans, Halle, 1773)
* Προγύμνασμα γεωμετρικόν, ήτοι νέα θεωρία τετραγωνισμού του κύκλου, (Introduction to Geometry: new theory of squaring the circle, 1774)
* Έπος ηρωελεγείον προς Αικατερίνη Β΄, (Honorary poem to Empress Catherine II, Leyden, 1776)
* Έπη δύο (Lugduni Batanorum), (Two Epics, Leyden, 1776)
* Ποίημα σαπφικόν εις τον ελλογιμώτατον και ευγενέστατον Σκαρλάτον τον Στούρλαν, (Sapphic poem to scholar and gentleman Scarlato Sturla, Vienna, 1777)
* Επίγραμμα ηρωελεγείον εις τον ιερομονάχοις... εφημέριον Άνθιμον..., (Honorary epigram to monk and priest Antimos, Vienna)
* Έπος σαπφικόν εις την γενέθλιον ημέραν του βασιλέως των Πρώσσων Φρεδερίκου Β΄ (Sapphic poem for the birthday of King of Prussia, [[Frederick II of Prussia|Frederick II]])
* Δύο επιγράμματα προς τον ηγεμόνα Υψηλάντην, (Two Epigrams to lord Ipsilantis, Leipzig)

Translation from German to Greek:
* Γραμματική του Ρενίου

Translations from Ancient Greek to German:
* Κανόνας του ορθού και τιμίου βίου
* Κατήχησις του Πλάτωνος
